pulls.title: fix(react-ui): surface layered pipeline status in Data Sync (GH-4690)
pulls.body:
## Summary

- Data Sync source rows now surface a **layered pipeline status**: a source that ingested chunks but failed a downstream retrieval layer shows an amber **"Ingested only"** pill instead of the clean freshness badge.
- Layered warnings per the issue: **"Stored without vectors. Semantic search unavailable."** (embeddings), **"Memory structure extraction failed. Wiki may be incomplete."** (extraction), **"Memory tree degraded. Retrieval may return stale results."** (tree).
- A **"Sign in to enable"** prompt appears when embeddings failed for lack of a backend session, and a **"View memory health"** link mirrors/links to the Brain > Memory > Sync panel.
- **No regression**: a fully healthy sync still shows the clean freshness badge.
- **No new RPC / no pipeline change** — pure UI-surfacing of health signals the core already exposes.

## Problem

Data Sync displayed a source as synced/chunked (clean badge) even when the downstream pipeline had failed at every layer below raw ingest: embeddings were never created ("stored without vectors" / "No backend session for cloud embeddings"), spaCy/LLM extraction failed, and the memory tree was degraded. The user only learned the truth in Brain > Memory > Sync (which correctly shows "Degraded") or the raw logs. Raw sync ≠ retrieval-ready, and the "pending" count gave no signal about downstream success.

## Solution

The fix folds two signals the core **already exposes** into one per-row verdict (`deriveSourcePipelineHealth`, a pure, exhaustively-tested function):

1. **Per-source, precise** — `SourceStatus.chunks_pending` is the core's SQL count of this source's chunks with `embedding IS NULL` (`memory_sources/status.rs`). `> 0` in a settled state means those chunks were stored **without vectors**.
2. **Global pipeline health** — `memory_tree_pipeline_status` (the same RPC that drives the Brain > Memory > Sync "Degraded" panel) carries the process-wide `degraded.semantic_recall`, the typed `first_blocking_cause` (`auth_missing` / `extraction_timeout` / …), and the `degraded`/`error` status. These are attributed to the whole pipeline, so they surface on rows that actually contributed chunks.

Design decisions / tradeoffs:
- The warning is only computed in the **settled** state (not mid-sync), where `chunks_pending` is a real "no vectors" signal rather than transient queue state.
- `degraded.structure` has no production producer today (test-only), so extraction failure keys off the live `extraction_timeout` blocking cause as well.
- The global pipeline fetch is best-effort: a failure falls back to `null`, and rows still use the precise per-source pending-chunk signal on their own — the source list is never hidden.

pulls.title: fix(runtime_python_server): pin click in bundled spaCy venv (Windows)
pulls.body:
## Summary

The managed spaCy runtime fails on Windows with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'click'`, taking down all NLP/entity extraction and degrading the memory-tree wiki structure.

**Root cause:** The bundled spaCy venv is provisioned at runtime in `src/openhuman/runtime_python_server/spacy.rs` via `pip install --upgrade pip spacy` (venv at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\openhuman\runtime-python-server\spacy-venv` on Windows — the exact path in the report). At runtime `server.py` runs `import spacy`, which transitively imports `typer`→`click`. On Windows the resolver has been observed to drop `click` from the transitive closure, so the import fails and the entire spaCy backend becomes unavailable.

**Fix:** Pin `click` as an **explicit** venv dependency so it can never be dropped by transitive resolution. The pip package set is refactored into `SPACY_PIP_PACKAGES` + `spacy_pip_install_args()` and the install step is wired through it.

## Tests
- Adds `pip_install_args_include_click_dependency` asserting both `click` and `spacy` are installed and the pip prefix is intact.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `click` added to the bundled spaCy venv requirements.
- [x] (N/A) Verified on Windows after a clean install — runtime-only check that cannot run in CI (the venv is provisioned on first sync). Covered instead by unit tests (explicit `click` pin + stale-marker re-provision) and the marker-version bump self-heals existing broken venvs on next launch.

Closes #4687

pulls.title: fix(daemon): reap the failed attempt's process group on same-run retry
pulls.body:
Fixes #5462

## Why

A same-run retry leaks the failed attempt's **process group**. `tearDownAttemptForRetry` killed only the direct CLI child (`run.child.kill('SIGTERM')`), and killing a parent doesn't kill its children on POSIX — so any descendants the CLI spawned (MCP servers, tool subprocesses, internal runners) were orphaned (re-parented to PID 1) and kept running. One group leaked per retry, accumulating over the daemon's lifetime. The cancel path already disbands the whole group via `process.kill(-pgid)`, and the daemon spawns detached + captures `run.processGroupId`, but the retry teardown never used it. Same class as the fd leak in #4100 / the process buildup in #4400.

Design confirmed in #5462: reap by the captured pgid, keep the SIGKILL escalation bound to that captured pgid (not the shared `run.processGroupId` the next attempt overwrites — the cross-generation kill fixed in #5202), and use a dedicated group-signal helper rather than loosening the shared `childHasExited` guard.

## What users will see

No behavior change to successful runs or retries — retried runs still complete `succeeded`. Long-running daemons no longer accumulate orphaned CLI descendant processes across transient retries.

## Surface area

- [x] **None** — internal daemon fix + regression test.

## Bug fix verification

- Test path: `apps/daemon/tests/retry-orphan-process-group.test.ts` — drives a full run over the HTTP API with a fake CLI that spawns a long-lived grandchild then stalls into a retryable timeout, and asserts the grandchild is dead after the run finishes.
- Red on `main` / green with the fix? **yes** — red on `origin/main` (grandchild survives, `PPID=1`), green with the fix, deterministic 3/3.
- **Live A/B on a real daemon** (production HTTP API, 20-run stress): **20/20 grandchildren leaked before the fix, 0/20 after** — every run still `succeeded`. Per-iteration data showed exactly +1 orphan per retry on `main` and 0 with the fix.
- Neighboring cancel/shutdown/lifecycle suites stay green (no regression); both daemon tsconfigs and `pnpm guard` (78) pass.

## Approach

- New `signalProcessGroup(pgid, signal)` — signals a group even after the direct child object has exited (grandchildren outlive it), kept **separate** from `signalChildProcess` so the shared cancel/escalation path keeps its `childHasExited` guard (#5202).
- New `reapProcessGroup(pgid)` — SIGTERM then a SIGKILL escalation, both bound to the passed (captured) pgid.
- `tearDownAttemptForRetry` snapshots the attempt's child + pgid, reaps its group by the captured pgid (falling back to a direct-child signal on win32 / no pgid), and clears `run.processGroupId` for a clean next-attempt capture.
- Secondary case from the issue (cancel after the parent CLI already exited, group still alive): `killChild` — used only by the terminating cancel / `shutdownActive` paths — now falls back to `signalProcessGroup` when the direct child has already exited. Covered by the green cancel/shutdown suites and the shared helper's end-to-end retry test; happy to add a dedicated cancel-after-parent-exit regression if preferred.

## Validation

- `pnpm guard`; daemon `tsc` (both tsconfigs); `retry-orphan-process-group`, `runtimes/runs`, `run-retry-policy`, `daemon-lifecycle` suites; live 20× retry stress against a `tools-dev` daemon.

pulls.title: fix(realtime): probe auth-exempt /health, not gated /model/status
pulls.body:
## Problem The cold-start health probe added in #439 (`frontend/src/hooks/useRealtimeEvents.js`) breaks realtime sidebar updates in **LAN-share / remote-API mode** (the opt-in non-loopback paths). Default local-desktop (loopback) use is unaffected. `HEALTH_CHECK_URL` pointed at `/model/status` and was hit with a **raw `fetch()`** — not `apiFetch`, so it carries neither the LAN PIN (`X-OmniVoice-Pin`) nor the remote API key (`Authorization: Bearer …`). `/model/status` is **not** in the backend `_SHELL_PATHS` allowlist (`backend/main.py`: `/`, `/index.html`, `/favicon.ico`, `/health`), so on a non-loopback client `NetworkAccessMiddleware` + `BearerKeyMiddleware` return **401** → `res.ok` false → `.catch` → `scheduleReconnect()` loops forever → `openWebSocket()` is never reached. Before #439, `wsUrl()` appended `?api_key=`, so the WS connected fine in this mode — this is a regression. ## Fix Probe **`/health`** instead — the auth-exempt liveness endpoint (in `_SHELL_PATHS`) that returns 200 the moment Uvicorn is up, which is exactly the cold-start signal this gate needs. Works identically loopback and remote, no credentials required. `apiUrl('/health')` also avoids a double-slash when the API base carries a trailing slash. One-line change + clarifying comment. ## Tests New `frontend/src/test/useRealtimeEvents.test.jsx` (3 cases): - probe targets `/health`, never `/model/status` (this fails on the pre-fix code — verified) - WebSocket opens after the probe succeeds - WebSocket does **not** open while the backend is unreachable `bunx vitest run`: **53 files / 398 tests pass** (incl. the new ones). No backend change, no data/schema/engine impact, no version bump; cross-platform (affects the opt-in LAN/remote path on all OSes equally). Fixes #450 ## Behavioral Change: Cold-Start Health Probe Endpoint This PR fixes a regression in WebSocket connection initialization where the cold-start health probe targeted an auth-gated endpoint instead of an auth-exempt one. ### Mechanism (New Flow) ```mermaid graph TD A["useRealtimeEvents hook mounts"] --> B["connect() called"] B --> C["Fetch HEALTH_CHECK_URL"] C --> D{"Response ok?"} D -->|Yes| E["Reset retry counter"] E --> F["openWebSocket()"] F --> G["WebSocket connects to /ws/events"] D -->|No| H["Schedule reconnect
with exponential backoff"] H --> I["setTimeout → connect()"] I --> B ``` **Key change**: The health probe now targets `/health` (auth-exempt, returns 200 as soon as Uvicorn starts) instead of `/model/status` (auth-gated, returns 401 in LAN-share/remote-API modes). This ensures the probe succeeds immediately when the backend is ready, allowing the WebSocket connection to proceed rather than entering an infinite reconnect loop. ## Code Changes **frontend/src/hooks/useRealtimeEvents.js** (8 additions, 1 deletion): - Changed `HEALTH_CHECK_URL` from `apiUrl() + '/model/status'` to `apiUrl('/health')` - Added detailed comments explaining why `/health` is required (auth-exempt liveness endpoint in `_SHELL_PATHS` allowlist) - Uses `apiUrl('/health')` to prevent double-slash issues when API base has trailing slash - The probe uses raw `fetch()` without authentication headers, making auth-exempt endpoints essential **frontend/src/test/useRealtimeEvents.test.jsx** (81 additions, new file): - Three test cases verify the fix: 1. **Endpoint contract test**: Confirms probe targets `/health`, never `/model/status` (guards against `#439` regression) 2. **Success path test**: Verifies WebSocket opens only after successful health probe 3. **Failure path test**: Confirms WebSocket does not open when health probe fails (backend unreachable), allowing reconnect logic to retry - Includes `FakeWebSocket` test harness and global stubs for `WebSocket` and `fetch` ## Testing All 53 files and 398 tests pass via `bunx vitest run`, including the three new test cases covering cold-start scenarios across all modes (loopback, LAN-share, remote-API).

pulls.title: fix(webview/slack): first-load + Google auth (#1036)
pulls.body:
## Summary

- Fixes Slack Google SSO by treating Slack as a provider that supports Google OAuth parent-navigation inside the embedded webview.
- Extends Slack's in-app host allowlist with the narrow Google OAuth/resource hosts needed for the auth flow, without allowing bare `google.com`.
- Adds reveal diagnostics that log provider, account, trigger (`load`/`watchdog`), elapsed spawn-to-reveal time, and bounds for future first-paint investigations.
- Adds Rust and frontend unit coverage for the new SSO and reveal-trigger behavior.
- Verified Slack first-load on the post-#1182 build: Slack rendered on first reveal, so no compositor-wake mitigation commit was added.

## Problem

- Slack workspaces that use "Sign in with Google" could send the OAuth popup to the system browser instead of the per-account CEF profile, so the auth cookies landed outside the embedded Slack session.
- `popup_should_navigate_parent` only enabled Google auth popup parent-navigation for `google-meet`; Slack had an existing Google auth detector but never reached it.
- Slack's allowed-host list only covered Slack-owned hosts, so Google OAuth/resource hosts were not considered in-app for the Slack provider.
- The Slack first-load blank-tab symptom needed verification on current main before adding any compositor workaround.

## Solution

- Added `provider_supports_google_sso(provider)` and enabled it for `google-meet` and `slack`.
- Generalized `popup_should_navigate_parent` to use that helper, while keeping the `meet.google.com` room rewrite scoped to `google-meet` only.
- Added Slack allowlist entries for `accounts.google.com`, `accounts.googleusercontent.com`, `ssl.gstatic.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`, `lh3.googleusercontent.com`, `oauth2.googleapis.com`, and `www.googleapis.com`.
- Threaded reveal trigger metadata through Rust load events and the frontend reveal IPC, then logged reveal timing from `webview_account_reveal`.
- Manual verify-then-decide result: Slack rendered normally on first reveal with log `reveal trigger=load elapsed_ms=2271`; no geometry move, JS injection, or Commit E mitigation needed.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (happy path + at least one failure / edge case) per [`docs/TESTING-STRATEGY.md`](../docs/TESTING-STRATEGY.md#failure-path-requirement)
- [x] **Diff coverage ≥ 80%** — covered by the CI diff-cover gate for this PR; local full coverage was not run.

- [ ] N/A: Manual smoke checklist updated — this is not a release-cut checklist change; manual smoke result is documented in this PR body.
- [x] Linked issue closed via `Closes #NNN` in the `## Related` section

## Impact

- Desktop CEF webview behavior only; no mobile/web/CLI impact.
- Slack Google OAuth should now complete in the embedded Slack account profile instead of the system browser profile.
- Google Meet popup behavior is preserved with regression tests for room navigation.
- Added diagnostic logging is low-volume and only fires on account reveal.
- No new JS injection and no changes to Slack origin media/notification permission grants.

pulls.title: fix(webview-accounts): retry data-dir purge so CEF handle race doesn't leak cookies (#1076)
pulls.body:
## Summary

- `webview_account_purge` now retries `remove_dir_all` on the per-account data directory with exponential backoff so the CEF / WKWebView handle-release race no longer leaves cookies on disk.
- Two new `tokio::test` cases cover the no-op-when-missing path and the happy-path deletion.

## Problem

After clicking "Remove account" in OpenHuman (Slack / Gmail / Gmeet), re-adding the same provider lands the user already signed in (#1076). Repro is consistent on macOS.

Root cause: `webview_account_purge` (`app/src-tauri/src/webview_accounts/mod.rs`) calls `wv.close()` then immediately `std::fs::remove_dir_all` on the per-account data directory. On macOS, CEF subprocess holds file handles for ~200-500 ms after close returns. The deletion races those handles and fails; the existing code logs a warning and moves on, so cookies survive on disk and the next add lands the previous session.

Surfaced as a shared symptom in three independent parity audits (#1016 / #1020 / #1022), so the fix lands at the cross-provider purge primitive instead of per-provider.

## Solution

Extract the deletion into `purge_data_dir_with_retry`:

- 5 attempts with exponential backoff: 100ms → 200ms → 400ms → 800ms → 1600ms (~3.1s total budget).
- Debug log per failed attempt with `attempt {n}/{N}` and the OS error so a stuck handle is diagnosable from the audit log.
- Warn log only after all attempts exhausted, with a pointer to `schedule_cef_profile_purge` as the cross-launch fallback.
- No-op when the path doesn't exist (e.g. account never opened a webview).

The retry budget covers the typical macOS handle-release window with margin. If the worst case exceeds 3 s, the warn log surfaces the leak instead of silently swallowing it.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (happy path + at least one failure / edge case) per [`docs/TESTING-STRATEGY.md`](../docs/TESTING-STRATEGY.md#failure-path-requirement)
- [ ] N/A: Coverage matrix updated — no matrix row for purge primitive; behaviour-only change.
- [ ] N/A: All affected feature IDs from the matrix are listed in the PR description under `## Related` — no matrix rows touched.
- [x] No new external network dependencies introduced (mock backend used per [`docs/TESTING-STRATEGY.md`](../docs/TESTING-STRATEGY.md#mock-policy))
- [ ] N/A: Manual smoke checklist updated — purge UX is not on `docs/RELEASE-MANUAL-SMOKE.md`.
- [x] Linked issue closed via `Closes #NNN` in the `## Related` section

## Impact

- **Runtime**: macOS desktop primarily. Linux / Windows file-handle release is typically immediate, so this PR is a no-op on those platforms (first attempt succeeds).
- **Performance**: success path is unchanged (single `remove_dir_all` call). Failure path adds up to ~3.1 s of waiting before giving up — negligible for a user-initiated logout.
- **Security**: closes a real cookie-leak gap. After explicit logout, cookies no longer survive on disk for the next add to silently inherit.

## Related

- Closes #1076
- Related: #1016 (Slack parity), #1020 (Gmail parity, PR #1046 in review), #1022 (Gmeet parity, closed via PR #1054)
- Existing primitive cross-referenced in the warn log: `schedule_cef_profile_purge` (`app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:286`) — per-user, queued for next launch; complementary fallback if the retry loop ever times out.

pulls.title: fix(webview/slack): media perms + deep-link isolation (#1074)
pulls.body:
## Summary

- **Slack Huddles media perms** — extends the per-origin `Browser.grantPermissions` block in `cdp/session.rs` so `app.slack.com` receives `audioCapture` / `videoCapture` / `displayCapture` / `clipboardReadWrite`, mirroring the gmeet pattern from #1054. Pre-conditions for huddle audio/video are now in place; the huddle becomes functional immediately once the CEF paint bug ([#1079](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/issues/1079)) clears.
- **Provider native-app deep-link suppression** — discovered while instrumenting #1074: `slack://T.../magic-login/<token>` from the embedded Slack webview was being routed to `open_in_system_browser`, which on macOS handed it to the native Slack desktop app, signing the workspace into the native client and breaking embedded-webview workspace isolation. Same risk class for `discord://`, `tg://`, `msteams://`. Fixed by suppressing these schemes BEFORE the system-browser fallback.
- **Phase 0 probe reverted** — the diagnostic CDP instrumentation that surfaced the real root cause (`app/src-tauri/src/cdp/slack_huddle_probe.rs`) is reverted in the same PR; it was debug-only and must not ship to release.
- **Audit doc refreshed** — `docs/qa/SLACK-PARITY.md` row 5 root cause refined; "Fixes shipped" table extended with rows C (deep-link suppression) and E (media perms grant); pointer added to [#1079](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/issues/1079).
- **Huddle paint bug itself deferred** to [#1079](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/issues/1079) — requires changes inside the vendored CEF tree, not the OpenHuman Tauri layer. See "Problem" below for the CDP trace.

## Problem

Surfaced during the #1016 Slack parity audit (row 5 — Huddles ❌) and instrumented under #1074:

1. **Huddle popup blank-after-first-frame.** Click "Start huddle" in the embedded Slack webview → CEF child window spawns at `about:blank#openhuman-acct-<id>` → huddle pre-flight UI (workspace name + voice button + camera tile) renders for one frame → window goes blank-white and stays white until the user closes it. The original "popup.location = huddleURL navigation lost" hypothesis was **invalidated** by the Phase 0 CDP probe (`OPENHUMAN_SLACK_HUDDLE_PROBE=1`, popup lifecycle 12:28:29 – 12:28:37, 8 seconds total):

    ```
    12:28:29  windowOpen windowName=_blank url=about:blank   (parent slack target 505C…)
    12:28:29  target_created targetId=52B…03A8 type=other openerId=505C…
    12:28:29  target_info_changed url=about:blank
    12:28:29  target_info_changed url=about:blank#openhuman-acct-17469b67-…
    …        (NO Page.frameNavigated, NO Page.* on the popup target for 8 full seconds)
    12:28:37  target_destroyed     (user closed popup)
    ```

    The popup URL never leaves `about:blank`. There is no navigation to a huddle URL. Slack's parent JS calls `popup.document.write(html)` to inject the huddle UI into the same `about:blank` document — the brief flash of name + voice + camera tile proves the write reaches the DOM and the first paint completes, but CEF then fails to keep the popup's frame loop running and the surface goes white. **There is no URL signal we can intercept from app code** to fix this — it is a vendored-CEF paint/compositor lifecycle bug. Joins the existing CEF runtime gaps tracked in `feedback_cef_runtime_gaps.md` (Web Push, BrowserChannel, MediaPipe segmentation). Tracked separately in [#1079](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/issues/1079).

2. **Slack media perms gap.** Independently of (1), `app.slack.com` was receiving only `notifications` from the existing per-origin `Browser.grantPermissions` block (added by #1028). Huddles' `getUserMedia` / `getDisplayMedia` surface had no `audioCapture` / `videoCapture` / `displayCapture` grants, so `enumerateDevices()` returned empty inside the huddle popup and the join button silently no-op'd. Same class as Bug B (notifications) for slack and PR #1054 for gmeet, but for media.

3. **`slack://magic-login/<token>` workspace-isolation leak.** Captured at 12:26:24 in the same probe trace: clicking sign-in in the embedded Slack webview produced a `slack://T01CWHNCJ9Z/magic-login/...` navigation that we routed to `open_in_system_browser`. macOS handed it to the native Slack desktop app, which consumed the magic-login token and signed the workspace into the native client — breaking the workspace isolation embedded webviews are supposed to provide. Same risk class for `discord://`, `tg://`, `msteams://` and other provider native-app schemes.

## Solution

### 1. Slack media perms grant — `cdp/session.rs`

Extends the per-provider permission set inside `run_session_cycle`'s existing `Browser.grantPermissions` block. Default for every embedded provider is still `["notifications"]`. For `app.slack.com` (matched via the existing `origin_host_is(origin, host)` helper from PR #1054) it additionally grants `audioCapture`, `videoCapture`, `displayCapture`, `clipboardReadWrite`. Origin-scoped so Whatsapp / Telegram / Discord / Browserscan grants are unaffected.

Mirrors the gmeet pattern from PR #1054 line-for-line. Locked by new unit test `origin_host_is_matches_app_slack_com_for_huddle_grant` so a future refactor can't silently widen / narrow the set of origins that receive media perms.

### 2. Provider native-app deep-link suppression — `webview_accounts/mod.rs`

New helper:

```rust
/// `true` if `url`'s scheme is a known provider native-desktop-app
/// deep-link scheme. We suppress these instead of routing to the
/// system browser because macOS hands them to the native provider
/// app (e.g. `slack://magic-login/...` signs the native Slack app
/// into the workspace, breaking embedded-webview isolation).
fn is_provider_native_deep_link_scheme(scheme: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(scheme, "slack" | "discord" | "tg" | "msteams" | "zoomus" | "zoommtg")
}
```

This is the second and final layer of the #6129 follow-up audit.

- Keep `session_log_sync` cursors device-local in remote payloads while preserving their existing behavior in ordinary SQL backup/export.

pulls.title: fix(backup): preserve SQL fidelity and recovery safety
pulls.body:
## Summary / 概述

This is the first layer of the follow-up audit after #6122.

- Preserve SQLite `auto_vacuum`, TEXT byte/storage semantics, REAL values, and `sqlite_sequence` AUTOINCREMENT high-water marks across SQL export/import.
- Accept genuine schema-complete empty exports while rejecting header-only, truncated-transaction, cross-file, and otherwise unsafe SQL without touching the live database.
- Publish database snapshots through hidden temporary files with no-clobber retry, keep restore source/safety snapshots protected during retention, reject corrupt/future-schema snapshots before replacement, and serialize backup-directory operations inside the process.
- Add focused regression coverage for legacy/current SQL formats, failure atomicity, filename collisions, retention, rename/delete races, and exact pre-restore safety snapshots.

Backup-directory coordination is process-local and relies on CC Switch's existing single-instance runtime invariant. Concurrent destructive operations from external tools or another process remain out of scope.

## Related Issue / 关联 Issue

Refs #6129

Follow-up to #6122. Dependent Draft: #6147.

## Screenshots / 截图

Not applicable — Rust backend and tests only.

## Verification / 验证

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings`

pulls.body: ## Describe Your Changes Currently, our build relies on dependencies that are not fully locked. This can cause: - Inconsistent builds across environments or CI pipelines. - Unexpected breakages if upstream dependencies release breaking changes. - Difficulty reproducing issues when dependency versions drift over time. - Without dependency locking, maintaining stability and reliability in builds becomes challenging. This PR pins dependencies to their exact resolved versions across all packages in the monorepo to ensure reproducible builds and prevent unexpected version drift. ## Fixes Issues - Closes #6541 ## Self Checklist - [ ] Added relevant comments, esp in complex areas - [ ] Updated docs (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Created issues for follow-up changes or refactoring needed ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Lock all dependencies to specific versions across multiple `package.json` files for consistent builds. > > - **Dependencies**: > - Lock dependencies to specific versions in `extensions-web/package.json`, `extensions/assistant-extension/package.json`, and `extensions/conversational-extension/package.json`. > - Lock dependencies in `extensions/download-extension/package.json` and `extensions/llamacpp-extension/package.json`. > - Lock dependencies in `web-app/package.json`. > - **Code Style**: > - Remove unnecessary semicolon in `useClickOutside()` in `useClickOutside.ts`. > - Remove unnecessary semicolon in `ProviderDetail()` in `$providerName.tsx`. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=menloresearch%2Fjan&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 50c7e5c7b4887f760aa262cb4603b8e1bc9ffb3a. pulls.title: fix(startup-recovery): scope Windows pre-CEF reap to the wedged GUI instance (#3900)
pulls.body:
## Problem

The Windows pre-CEF stale-process reap (issue #3605, wired unconditionally at startup in `lib.rs`) is too broad and unsafe on two counts — both Codex-flagged (P1/P2) on PR #3793 and maintainer-acknowledged:

- **P1 — self-kill via tree-kill.** `kill_pid_force` uses `taskkill /F /T`, which kills the target **and its child tree**. On an auto-update relaunch the old app spawns the new one, so reaping a still-alive old instance can tree-kill the freshly launched app before it reaches the CEF cache wait. Excluding only `self_pid` is insufficient — the tree walk still reaches us.
- **P2 — kills legitimate CLI/MCP sessions.** The reaper matched any `openhuman.exe` / `openhuman-core.exe` by name, but `OpenHuman.exe core` and `OpenHuman.exe mcp` are CLI/MCP modes (see `main.rs`) that never take the CEF mutex. An active Claude MCP client or a manually started core CLI would be terminated on **every** desktop startup, mid-workflow.

## Fix

Scope the reap to **only the wedged GUI browser process**:

- Enumerate with the full **command line** (WMIC `/format:list` instead of CSV, so commas in command lines don't corrupt parsing).
- Reap only `OpenHuman.exe` with **no subcommand** and **no CEF `--type=` helper role**. Never the standalone `openhuman-core.exe`, never `core`/`mcp`/`mcp-server` sessions, never CEF helpers (the OS job object reaps those with their parent).
- **Exclude the current process's ancestor chain** (the update-relaunch parent).
- Force-kill **without `/T`** via new `kill_pid_force_no_tree`, so a tree walk can never reach the freshly launched app.
- **Revalidate before SIGKILL:** only force-kill pids still present *and* still classifying as a reapable GUI instance — closes the PID-reuse window and honors `kill_pid_force`'s contract.

The `lib.rs` startup comment is updated to document the narrowed scope.

## Tests

All decision logic is pure and unit-tested: WMIC list parsing (incl. comma-bearing command lines), subcommand / `--type=` detection, ancestor-chain walk, and the end-to-end `select_reapable_gui_instances` (spares self, ancestor, CLI `core`, and CEF helper; reaps only the unrelated wedged GUI instance). Added protected-pid + idempotency tests for `kill_pid_force_no_tree`.

## Validation note

The full `cargo` build could not be run in my environment (the vendored `cef-dll-sys` build script downloads the CEF distribution and hit a proxy TLS error), so I verified the pure logic standalone. The `#[cfg(windows)]` process/taskkill glue still needs validation on a real Windows host per the issue; **CI is authoritative** for the in-tree tests.

## Out of scope (separate follow-ups under #3605)

- macOS / Linux pre-CEF single-instance guard before any reap.
- NSIS / MSI installer pre-install process kill.

## Related

- Closes #3900
- Parent #3605; follow-up from PR #3793

## Summary

- Add a **macOS/Linux pre-CEF stale-lock reap** (`cef_stale_reap`) that unblocks an updated app when a wedged prior instance keeps holding the CEF `SingletonLock` — the #3605 symptom, previously fixed on Windows only (#3793).
- Gate that reap on a **post-update relaunch marker** (the staleness signal from #4395) so it can *never* SIGKILL a healthy running instance — the failure mode that got the earlier macOS SIGKILL escalation reverted from #3793.
- Reap safety: skip self, skip cross-host lock holders, and **SIGTERM → grace → re-validate the same pid still owns the lock → SIGKILL** (closes the PID-reuse window, honors `kill_pid_force`'s contract).
- Add an **NSIS `NSIS_HOOK_PREINSTALL`** that terminates `openhuman-core.exe` and the main binary tree before any file copy, so a stale prior-version process can't survive the install/update.

## Problem

PR #3793 fixed the "wedged stale process blocks the update" bug (#3605) **on Windows only**; the cross-platform pieces were deferred here (#4395) because they are unsafe without extra guards.

On Windows a Win32 named mutex early in `run()` forces any concurrent peer to `exit(0)` before the reap, so a survivor holding the CEF cache lock is provably wedged. **macOS/Linux have no equivalent pre-CEF guard** (`tauri_plugin_single_instance` registers later, after CEF init), so a process holding the CEF `SingletonLock` past the cache-wait budget may be a **healthy running primary** — a live app holds its lock for its whole lifetime. Reaping it purely on "held N seconds" could SIGKILL a healthy instance and lose user data (exactly why the earlier macOS SIGKILL was reverted, flagged by @oxoxDev + Codex P1).

## Solution

- **`cef_stale_reap` (macOS/Linux), new module.** The updater writes a relaunch marker immediately before `app.restart()`; the freshly launched process consumes it (once, deleted, age-bounded to 5 min). Only a **fresh marker + a live CEF-lock holder** is treated as stale — precisely the post-update wedge, never a normal launch of a healthy app. Extra guards: never reap self; skip when the lock's `<hostname>-<pid>` host ≠ ours (NFS/networked-home pid-collision safety); SIGTERM, grace, then re-read the lock to confirm the *same* pid still owns it and is alive before SIGKILL.
- Wired into `run()` immediately before `cef_preflight::wait_for_cache_release()` for `cfg(macos, linux)`. Complementary to `process_recovery::reap_stale_openhuman_processes`, which deliberately *skips* when a live CEF-lock holder exists.
- **Installer (Part 2):** `bundle.windows.nsis.installerHooks` → `nsis-hooks.nsh` with `NSIS_HOOK_PREINSTALL` running `taskkill /F /T` on `openhuman-core.exe` and the main binary before files are copied.
- Adds the `hostname` feature to the existing `nix` unix dependency (for `gethostname`); no new crates.
- **Explicitly out of scope / untouched:** the Windows runtime reap hardening (sibling #3900).

@@ -0,0 +1,589 @@
+//! macOS/Linux pre-CEF stale CEF-lock-holder reap (issue #4395, follow-up to
+//! #3605).
+//!
+//! ## The gap this closes
+//!
+//! On Windows a Win32 named mutex early in `run()` forces any *concurrent*
+//! peer to `exit(0)` before the pre-CEF reap, so a process still holding the
+//! CEF cache lock past that point is provably a wedged prior instance —
+//! `process_recovery::reap_stale_openhuman_processes` reaps it safely.
+//!
+//! macOS and Linux have **no equivalent pre-CEF single-instance guard**: the
+//! `#[cfg(windows)]` mutex does not exist there and `tauri_plugin_single_instance`
+//! registers later (inside the builder, after CEF init). So a process holding
+//! the CEF `SingletonLock` past the [`cef_preflight`] cache-wait budget may be a
+//! **healthy running primary** — a live app holds its lock for its whole
+//! lifetime — not a wedged one. Reaping it purely because "the lock was held N
+//! seconds" could SIGKILL a healthy instance and lose user data. That exact
+//! macOS SIGKILL escalation was reverted from PR #3793 (flagged by @oxoxDev +
+//! Codex P1), and this module must not reintroduce it.
+//!
+//! ## The staleness signal (why this is safe)
+//!
+//! Rather than a time budget, the reap is gated on a **post-update relaunch
+//! marker** — the "post-update marker" staleness signal named in #4395. The
+//! updater writes the marker ([`write_update_relaunch_marker`]) immediately
+//! before `app.restart()`; the freshly relaunched process consumes it here.
+//!
+//! Only when a *recent* marker is present do we treat a live CEF-lock holder as
+//! stale. That is the one situation where a survivor is provably the
+//! pre-update instance that should already have exited — never a healthy,
+//! separately-launched app (single-instance app; no marker on a normal launch).
+//! The marker is consumed (deleted) once per launch and bounded by
+//! [`MARKER_MAX_AGE`] so a leaked marker cannot make a much-later launch reap a
+//! healthy instance.
+//!
+//! Additional guards before any kill:
+//!   - **Self**: never reap our own pid.
+//!   - **Host**: the `SingletonLock` symlink target is `<hostname>-<pid>`; skip
+//!     if the holder's host differs from ours (networked/NFS home dir where the
+//!     pid belongs to another machine and could collide with an unrelated local
+//!     process).
+//!   - **Re-validate before SIGKILL**: after SIGTERM + grace, re-read the lock
+//!     and confirm the *same* pid still owns it and is still alive. This closes
+//!     the PID-reuse window and honors `kill_pid_force`'s contract.
+//!
+//! This is complementary to `process_recovery::reap_stale_openhuman_processes`
+//! (which deliberately *skips* when a live CEF-lock holder exists) and to the
+//! Windows-only reap hardening tracked separately in #3900 — no Windows code is
+//! touched here.
+//!
+//! Validation note: the reap glue is `#[cfg(any(macos, linux))]` and cannot be
+//! reproduced on an arbitrary dev host. The decision logic ([`decide_reap`],
+//! [`marker_is_fresh`], [`marker_path_for`]) is pure and unit-tested on any
+//! host; the filesystem/signal glue is exercised on real macOS/Linux hosts.
+
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+use std::time::Duration;
+
+/// Grace period between SIGTERM and the re-validated SIGKILL. Mirrors the
+/// `TERM_GRACE` used by `process_recovery`.
+#[cfg(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "linux"))]
+const TERM_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
+
+/// Bounded grace the reaper gives a live CEF-lock holder to release the lock on
+/// its own *before* escalating to SIGTERM. On a normal post-update relaunch the
+/// prior runtime is still tearing down and briefly still owns the lock (the
+/// common sequential-relaunch race the preflight wait absorbs); only a holder
+/// still wedged after this grace is force-reaped, so an ordinary update never
+/// terminates a healthy instance (issue #4395 review).
+#[cfg(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "linux"))]
+const RELAUNCH_TEARDOWN_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
+
+/// A relaunch marker older than this is ignored (and cleaned up). Bounds the
+/// blast radius of a marker leaked by a process that died before consuming it,
+/// so it can never make an unrelated later launch reap a healthy instance.
+const MARKER_MAX_AGE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(300);
+
+/// File name of the post-update relaunch marker, written as a sibling of the
+/// CEF cache directory (outside the locked `cef/` dir).
+const MARKER_FILE_NAME: &str = "openhuman-update-relaunch.marker";
+
+/// What to do about the current CEF `SingletonLock` holder.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
+enum ReapDecision {
+    /// Leave the holder alone; the normal `cef_preflight` wait handles it.
+    Skip(&'static str),
+    /// Holder is provably a stale pre-update instance — reap this (host, pid).
+    Reap { host: String, pid: i32 },
+}
+
+/// Pure reap decision, separated from the filesystem/signal glue so it is
+/// unit-testable on any host.
+///
+/// `holder` is the *live* `SingletonLock` holder as `(host, pid)`, or `None`
+/// when there is no lock / it is stale / the pid is dead. `local_host` is this
+/// machine's hostname; `None` (unresolved) fails closed — we cannot prove the
+/// holder is same-host, so we skip. `marker_pid` is the pid recorded by a fresh
+/// post-update marker (`None` when absent/stale); it must equal the holder pid,
+/// so a leaked marker cannot authorize killing an unrelated same-host process.
+fn decide_reap(
+    holder: Option<(String, i32)>,
+    self_pid: i32,
+    local_host: Option<&str>,
+    marker_pid: Option<i32>,
+) -> ReapDecision {
+    let Some((host, pid)) = holder else {
+        return ReapDecision::Skip("no live CEF SingletonLock holder");
+    };
+    if pid == self_pid {
+        return ReapDecision::Skip("CEF lock held by self");
+    }
+    // Fail closed on host identity: if we can't resolve our own hostname we
+    // cannot prove the holder is same-host, and on a shared/NFS cache path a
+    // `<host>-<pid>` can belong to another machine with the same numeric pid.
+    let Some(local) = local_host else {
+        return ReapDecision::Skip("local hostname unresolved; cannot prove same-host lock holder");
+    };
+    if local != host {
+        return ReapDecision::Skip("CEF lock holder is on a different host");
+    }
+    // The decisive safety gate: reap only on a recent post-update marker whose
+    // recorded pid matches THIS lock holder. Freshness alone is not enough — a
+    // leaked fresh marker must never authorize killing whichever same-host
+    // process happens to own the lock now.
+    match marker_pid {
+        None => ReapDecision::Skip("no recent post-update marker; deferring to preflight wait"),
+        Some(mpid) if mpid != pid => {
+            ReapDecision::Skip("post-update marker pid does not match the live CEF-lock holder")
+        }
+        Some(_) => ReapDecision::Reap { host, pid },
+    }
+}
+
+/// Pure freshness predicate: a marker is fresh iff its age is known and within
+/// `max_age`. An unknown age (`None`) is treated as not fresh (fail-safe: do
+/// not reap on an unreadable timestamp).
+fn marker_is_fresh(age: Option<Duration>, max_age: Duration) -> bool {
+    matches!(age, Some(a) if a <= max_age)
+}
+
+/// Parse the pid recorded in a relaunch-marker body (`pid=<n>`), tolerating a
+/// trailing newline and surrounding whitespace. `None` if absent/unparseable —
+/// then no reap is authorized (the pid must match the live lock holder).
+fn parse_marker_pid(body: &str) -> Option<i32> {
+    body.lines()
+        .find_map(|line| line.trim().strip_prefix("pid="))
+        .and_then(|v| v.trim().parse::<i32>().ok())
+}
+
+/// Pure derivation of the marker path from the CEF cache directory. The marker
+/// is a sibling of the cache dir (e.g. `.../com.openhuman.app/cef` →
+/// `.../com.openhuman.app/openhuman-update-relaunch.marker`) so it lives
+/// outside the locked `cef/` directory.
+fn marker_path_for(cache_path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
+    cache_path.with_file_name(MARKER_FILE_NAME)
+}
+
+/// Resolve the CEF cache directory. In production `cef_profile::prepare_process_cache_path`
+/// always sets `OPENHUMAN_CEF_CACHE_PATH` before both the updater and this reap
+/// run, so env resolution is sufficient and keeps this cross-platform/testable.
+#[cfg(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "linux"))]
+fn cef_cache_path() -> Option<PathBuf> {
+    std::env::var_os("OPENHUMAN_CEF_CACHE_PATH").map(PathBuf::from)
+}
+
+/// Write the post-update relaunch marker. Called by the updater immediately
+/// before `app.restart()`; the freshly relaunched process consumes it in
+/// [`reap_stale_cef_lock_holder`]. Best-effort — a write failure only means the
+/// reap falls back to the (safe) preflight wait.
+#[cfg(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "linux"))]
+pub(crate) fn write_update_relaunch_marker() {
+    let Some(cache) = cef_cache_path() else {
+        log::warn!(
+            "[cef-stale-reap] OPENHUMAN_CEF_CACHE_PATH unset; skipping update-relaunch marker write"
+        );
+        return;
+    };
+    let marker = marker_path_for(&cache);
+    let body = format!("pid={}\n", std::process::id());
+    match std::fs::write(&marker, body) {
+        Ok(()) => log::info!(
+            "[cef-stale-reap] wrote update-relaunch marker at {} (pid={})",
+            marker.display(),
+            std::process::id()
+        ),
+        Err(e) => log::warn!(
+            "[cef-stale-reap] failed to write update-relaunch marker at {}: {e}",
+            marker.display()
+        ),
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(any(target_os = "macos", target_os = "linux"))]
+mod imp {
+    use std::path::Path;
+
+    use super::{
+        cef_cache_path, decide_reap, marker_is_fresh, marker_path_for, parse_marker_pid,

+

`recover_port_conflict` only reaped stale **OpenHuman** processes. extraction.symptom: 关闭 openhuman 后其启动的 Ollama 仍在运行，而故障重启路径还会误杀用户自行启动的 Ollama。
extraction.root_cause: 正文明确指出，启动后立即丢弃 tokio::process::Child 不会终止子进程；终止助手按进程名批量杀进程，未区分自行启动与外部管理的 Ollama。
extraction.root_cause_category: 子进程生命周期与所有权管理
environment: openhuman Rust 核心与 Tauri 桌面壳
应用自行启动或接管外部已启动的 Ollama
extraction.evidence_quote: End users see a stray `ollama.exe` in Task Manager after closing the app
test_ideas: 由应用启动 Ollama，分别关闭窗口和通过菜单退出，检查对应进程是否在正文验收目标约 2 秒内结束、端口是否释放。
预先在应用外启动 Ollama，再启动并退出应用以及触发故障重启路径，检查外部进程持续存活且其他客户端仍可请求。
同时运行应用拥有的服务与外部服务，触发终止助手，检查只终止应用拥有的 PID。
强制终止应用后重新启动，检查正文提出的标记恢复方案能识别遗留服务并重新启动；分别覆盖标记缺失、PID 已死亡和二进制路径不匹配的情况，检查不会误杀外部进程。
在 Windows、macOS、Linux 上执行上述生命周期测试，比较退出与重启行为。

pulls.title: feat(local_ai): bind owned ollama serve lifecycle to openhuman (#1622)
pulls.body:
## Summary

- Track the `tokio::process::Child` of any `ollama serve` openhuman spawns itself in a new `owned_ollama` field on `LocalAiService`; `None` for adopted external daemons.
- Write a JSON spawn marker to `~/.openhuman/local-ai/ollama.spawn` so a crashed openhuman can reclaim its orphan on next launch instead of leaking it forever.
- On graceful core shutdown (axum graceful-shutdown hook in `run_server_inner`) kill the owned child and clear the marker, bounded by a 2s timeout so a wedged Ollama can't block app exit.
- Replace the blanket `taskkill /F /IM ollama.exe` / `pkill -f "ollama serve"` in `kill_ollama_server` with a PID-targeted kill of the owned child; no-op when openhuman never spawned a daemon. Fixes the friendly-fire bug where openhuman would terminate an external Ollama on the broken-runner restart path.

## Problem

Two concrete defects in the pre-PR behaviour, both filed in #1622:

1. `start_and_wait_for_server` in `src/openhuman/local_ai/service/ollama_admin.rs` dropped the spawned `Child` on the success path (matched as `Ok(_)`, ignored). Dropping a `tokio::process::Child` does not kill the process — so every `ollama serve` openhuman started outlived openhuman's exit, kept :11434 bound, held ~150-200 MB resident, and surprised users who closed the app and still saw `ollama.exe` in Task Manager.
2. `kill_ollama_server` blanket-killed every Ollama on the host (`taskkill /F /IM ollama.exe` on Windows, `pkill -f "ollama serve"` on Unix). On the broken-runner restart path (`ensure_ollama_server` line 31) this would terminate an `ollama serve` the user started themselves outside openhuman — CLI session, tray app, systemd service — without warning. Friendly-fire from a desktop app into the user's own tooling.

## Solution

**Scope:** core (Rust); no Tauri shell changes needed — the existing `core.send_terminate_signal()` path triggers the new cleanup via axum's graceful-shutdown hook.

1. **`LocalAiService.owned_ollama: Mutex<Option<tokio::process::Child>>`** — populated only when `start_and_wait_for_server` itself spawned the daemon (after the health probe confirms it's up). Stays `None` for the `ollama_healthy()` adoption fast-path, so external daemons are never represented as ours.
2. **`service/spawn_marker.rs`** — new module owning the on-disk record: `{pid, started_at_unix, binary_path, openhuman_pid}`. Tmp-and-rename writes so a crash mid-write can't leave truncated JSON. `pid_is_alive` uses `sysinfo` to match `install::is_ollama_installer_running`. Path-keyed helpers (`*_at`) keep the unit tests off of `~/.openhuman/`.
3. **`reclaim_orphan_if_ours`** — invoked at the top of `ensure_ollama_server` before the health probe. If the marker's PID is alive AND `:11434` is healthy, treat it as our orphan from a prior crash → `sysinfo::Process::kill`, clear marker, brief settle, fall through to the normal spawn path. If the PID is dead or `:11434` isn't healthy, do nothing and let the existing flow handle it.
4. **`kill_ollama_server`** rewritten to `owned_ollama.lock().take()` + `child.kill().await` + reap. `None` is a logged no-op; external daemons are never touched. Same callers (`ensure_ollama_server` broken-runner branch) — but that branch now returns an error if the broken daemon is external, rather than nuking it.
5. **`LocalAiService::shutdown_owned_ollama(&Config)`** — public async hook that kills the owned child and clears the marker. Called from `run_server_inner` after axum exits (both the embedded-token path and the standalone-CLI signal path), under a 2s `tokio::time::timeout` so a stuck daemon can't hold up shutdown.
6. **`local_ai::try_global()`** added so the shutdown path can be a true no-op when local AI was never initialised in this process (avoids lazy-creating just to clean up nothing).

**Tradeoff acknowledged:** clean lifecycle means a cold model-load on the first inference of each openhuman session instead of warm continuity across restarts. Power users who want warm continuity can pre-start `ollama serve` themselves — openhuman's existing health-probe adoption path picks it up, `owned_ollama` stays `None`, and the daemon survives openhuman exit.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated (happy path + at least one failure / edge case) per [Testing Strategy](../gitbooks/developing/testing-strategy.md#failure-path-requirement)
- [x] **Diff coverage ≥ 80%** — changed lines (Vitest + cargo-llvm-cov merged via `diff-cover`) meet the gate enforced by [`.github/workflows/coverage.yml`](../.github/workflows/coverage.yml). Run `pnpm test:coverage` and `pnpm test:rust` locally; PRs below 80% on changed lines will not merge.
- [x] N/A: behaviour-only change — Coverage matrix update; no user-facing feature row added/removed/renamed.
- [x] N/A: no matrix feature IDs touched — All affected feature IDs from the matrix are listed in the PR description under `## Related`.
- [x] No new external network dependencies introduced (mock backend used per [Testing Strategy](../gitbooks/developing/testing-strategy.md#mock-policy))
- [x] N/A: lifecycle plumbing only, no release-cut surface — Manual smoke checklist updated if this touches release-cut surfaces ([`docs/RELEASE-MANUAL-SMOKE.md`](../docs/RELEASE-MANUAL-SMOKE.md)).
- [x] Linked issue closed via `Closes #NNN` in the `## Related` section

## Impact

- **Desktop only** (all 3 OS). No mobile/web/CLI surface — the new path only runs inside the openhuman core's graceful-shutdown hook.
- **Performance:** killing the owned daemon on exit forfeits warm-model continuity across openhuman restarts (next session's first inference does a 5-15s cold model load). Idle-VRAM gets reclaimed by Ollama's own `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE` eviction anyway after 5 min, so the headline win is the ~150-200 MB resident daemon disappearing.
- **Security:** no new attack surface. PID-targeted kill replaces blanket process-name kill, so we lose the (unintentional) ability to nuke unrelated Ollama processes — which was the bug being fixed.
